name: Start up a project and turn it over from estimating
summary: When a contract is signed, the estimating team that priced the job hands it to the operations team that will build it. The operations manager staffs the project, the estimator walks the team through the bid, the project manager turns the estimate into a budget by cost code, and the job is set up in the ERP and the project platform. The superintendent walks the site and plans logistics, and the startup package launches buyout, safety planning, scheduling, permits and mobilization. It is slow because the estimator and the site staff are still busy on other jobs, and error-prone because assumptions and late scope changes from bid day are lost in the handover.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees building institutional, commercial and industrial buildings, with about 10 project starts a month across three regions.
baseline.notes: Budgets were re-cut from the estimate in Excel and keyed or imported into the ERP; the project platform (Procore-type) held documents and logs. Large P3 projects run a longer startup with a dedicated team and are at the high end of the ranges.

trigger: Business development passes on an executed contract (or a letter of intent with notice to proceed).
end_state: The operations manager releases the project to mobilize, with the team assigned, budget loaded, systems set up and the startup package issued to the departments that act on it; or the owner defers the start.

volume.seasonality: More starts are scheduled for March to June so foundations and structure are done before winter; fewer in December and January.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver project-starts (7-10-14 a month), derived from about $1.5B revenue and about 220 active projects.

surge.cause: spring start of the construction season, when owners release projects awarded over the winter

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the seasonal bunching of building starts in Canada.

systems.name: Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Open the startup file from the signed contract
steps.description: The operations manager receives the executed contract and award notice from business development by email, opens a startup folder on the document drive and records the project in the opportunity tracker as won. He checks the contract value, delivery model, start date and region to decide which office runs it.

error.defect_description: Wrong region or delivery model recorded.

next.condition: owner defers or cancels the start after award

evidence.note: Owners occasionally hold a start after award (funding, permits); 2% is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Choose the project manager and superintendent
steps.description: The operations manager compares the size, type and location of the job with the staff who are coming off other projects, then picks a project manager, superintendent, field engineer and assistant project manager. He weighs who knows the owner or building type against who is actually free in the next month.

error.defect_description: A superintendent is named who is still tied to closeout on another job.

evidence.note: Staffing from the bench of finishing projects is the usual practice; the wait reflects people still closing out other jobs.

steps.name: Approve the team and any outside hire
steps.description: The regional vice-president reviews the proposed team at the weekly operations meeting or by email, checks it against the project's risk and the region's other starts, and approves it or swaps a person. Where no one suitable is free he authorises a salaried hire.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority: regional vice-president approves project leadership appointments

next.condition: an outside or transfer hire is needed

evidence.note: Regional VP sign-off on project readiness is described in the Brinkmann process pages; approval of staffing by the same level is the author's assumption.

steps.name: Raise a hire request for the missing role
steps.description: The operations manager writes a hire request to HR naming the role, project, location, start date and salary band, and attaches the approval from the regional vice-president. Field engineers and assistant superintendents are the roles most often requested.

error.defect_description: Start date or salary band missing, so HR asks again.

evidence.note: 20% of starts needing at least one outside hire is the author's estimate for 2021-2022 labour markets.

steps.name: Assemble the estimating turnover package
steps.description: The estimator who priced the job pulls the final bid sheets, take-off files, trade bid tabulations, qualifications, exclusions, allowances, alternates and the bid-day scope sheets into one turnover folder. He writes a short memo on the assumptions behind general conditions, self-perform production rates and duration.

error.defect_description: Assumptions or late bid-day scope changes are left out of the memo.

evidence.note: Contents of the handover from the source; the estimator is usually already working on the next bid, which causes the wait.

steps.name: Read the contract against the bid
steps.description: The project manager reads the executed contract, supplementary conditions, specifications and addenda, and compares them with the bid qualifications and the turnover package. He lists clauses that change risk or cost: liquidated damages, holdback terms, owner-supplied items, phasing and any scope added during negotiation.

error.defect_description: A changed clause or added scope item is missed.

evidence.note: Scope drift between the proposal and the final contract is named as the main handoff failure.

steps.name: Book the turnover meeting
steps.description: The assistant project manager finds a half day when the estimator, project manager, superintendent, operations manager and project accountant are free, books a room or Teams call and circulates the turnover package beforehand.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Run the estimating to operations turnover meeting
steps.description: The estimator walks the project team through the estimate line by line: scope by trade, carried allowances, exclusions, self-perform quantities and rates, general conditions and the planned duration. The team challenges assumptions and records open questions and commitments made to the owner during the pursuit.

error.defect_description: A verbal commitment made to the owner is not written into the minutes.

evidence.note: Meeting content from the sources; length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review site logistics and constructability in the meeting
steps.description: In the same meeting the superintendent tests the estimate's crane, hoist, hoarding and site trailer allowances against how he would build the job, and flags sequence or access problems the estimate did not price. He notes items for the logistics plan.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Superintendent attendance at the turnover meeting is standard; counted as its own step because a second role's time is spent.

steps.name: Log gaps between the bid and the contract
steps.description: The project manager enters each open question, scope gap and contract difference in a turnover log with an owner and a cost estimate, and decides which ones need the estimator to explain or price before the budget can be set.

error.defect_description: A gap is logged without a cost, so the budget carries no allowance for it.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Answer open questions on the estimate
steps.description: The estimator goes back to the bid files and trade bids to explain how a disputed item was priced, which subcontractor's number carried it, or why it was excluded, and replies to the project manager by email with figures.

error.defect_description: Explanation refers to a superseded bid tab.

evidence.note: Estimators are usually committed to new bids, so answers take a few days.

steps.name: Build the project budget by cost code
steps.description: The project manager re-cuts the estimate into the company's cost code structure in an Excel budget template: one line per trade package, self-perform labour, material and equipment, general conditions, contingency and fee. He adds allowances for logged gaps and agrees the target margin with the bid margin.

error.defect_description: Lines mapped to the wrong cost code or a trade package double counted.

evidence.note: Re-cutting a bid into job cost codes in Excel was the common practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review and approve the budget and margin
steps.description: The operations manager compares the draft budget with the bid summary, checks that fee, contingency and general conditions match what was approved at bid, and questions lines that grew or shrank. He approves it for loading or sends it back with comments.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company project controls policy: original budget approved by operations manager before job cost loading

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Set up the job and load the budget in the ERP
steps.description: The project accountant creates the job number, customer, contract value, billing terms, 10% holdback and retention settings and the cost code list in the construction ERP, then imports the approved budget. She sets up the schedule of values skeleton for the first progress draw.

error.defect_description: Budget line keyed to the wrong cost code or holdback rate wrong.

evidence.note: Accounting setup from a new project setup form per the Brinkmann pages; schedule of values due 15 days before the first draw under CCDC 2 GC 5.2.4.

steps.name: Set up the project platform and document folders
steps.description: The assistant project manager creates the project in the project management platform, uploads the contract drawings and specifications, builds the directory of owner, consultant and team contacts, and opens empty RFI, submittal and meeting logs. She mirrors the folder structure on the document drive.

error.defect_description: An addendum is not uploaded, so the field builds from a superseded sheet.

steps.name: Send WSIB clearance and insurance certificates to the owner
steps.description: The assistant project manager downloads a current WSIB clearance certificate from the government portal, obtains the project insurance certificates from the risk department, and sends both to the owner and consultant as the contract requires before work starts.

error.defect_description: Certificate names the wrong owner entity.

control.basis: CCDC 2-2020 GC 10.4.1 (workers' compensation compliance before commencing the Work) and GC 11.1 insurance

steps.name: Drive to the site for the startup walk
steps.description: The superintendent drives from the regional office or his current job to the new site once the owner allows access, carrying the drawings, a camera and a measuring wheel.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Round trip of one to three hours is typical for regional jobs; access often waits for the owner to vacate or hand over the site.

steps.name: Walk the site and record existing conditions
steps.description: The superintendent walks the site and surroundings, photographs existing conditions and neighbouring buildings, checks access routes, overhead lines, utility locations, laydown space and where the trailer, crane and hoarding can go, and notes anything that differs from the drawings.

error.defect_description: An existing condition (buried service, sloped grade) is missed.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Draft the site logistics plan
steps.description: Back at the office the superintendent marks up a site plan with the trailer compound, hoarding line, gates, crane radius, hoist, laydown and traffic routes, and lists temporary services needed. The plan feeds mobilization, permits and the safety plan.

error.defect_description: Crane or hoarding location conflicts with a permit or neighbour constraint.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Prepare the buyout plan and procurement schedule
steps.description: The project manager lists every trade package and major material order with its budget, the bidders from tender, required award date and long-lead items, and sets the order in which packages must be bought out to support the schedule.

error.defect_description: A long-lead item is not flagged for early award.

evidence.note: Buyout log and long-lead identification right after award.

steps.name: Request self-perform crews and equipment
steps.description: The superintendent tells the self-perform group how many concrete, formwork and general labour crews, cranes and formwork sets the job needs and when, using the estimate quantities and his sequence, so crew planning can book them.

error.defect_description: Crew start date given before the subgrade will be ready.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Request site trailer IT and phones
steps.description: The assistant project manager raises an IT ticket for the site trailer: internet connection, printer, laptops or tablets for new staff and phone numbers, giving the address and the date the trailer arrives.

error.defect_description: Wrong install date.

evidence.note: General contractor practice for a $1-100M buildings project; durations are the author's estimate from how a turnover is usually run.

steps.name: Issue the startup package and hold the internal kickoff
steps.description: The project manager assembles the startup package (contract summary, budget, logistics plan, buyout plan, key dates and team list) and sends it to supply chain, scheduling, safety, environment and permits. He runs a kickoff with the site team and the operations manager to agree roles, risks and the first month's priorities.

error.defect_description: A department is left off the distribution and starts late.

evidence.note: Start-up and kickoff strategy meetings as described in the source.

steps.name: Attend the owner's pre-construction meeting
steps.description: The project manager meets the owner and consultant to confirm contacts, lines of communication, submittal and RFI procedures, draw dates, site access, owner-supplied items and the date the construction schedule is due.

error.defect_description: A procedure agreed verbally is not minuted.

evidence.note: Owner-called meeting; the wait depends on the consultant's calendar.

steps.name: Approve project readiness to mobilize
steps.description: The operations manager goes through the readiness checklist with the project manager: budget loaded, team assigned, insurance and WSIB sent, safety plan under way, permits applied for, first subcontracts in progress. He releases the job to mobilize or names items to close first.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company project readiness checklist sign-off before mobilization

evidence.note: The source has the regional VP approving readiness; in this organisation the operations manager signs and the VP is informed.

exceptions.name: Bid assumptions do not match the contract
exceptions.description: Scope added in negotiation or a qualification the owner struck out is found at turnover; the estimator has to explain the pricing before the budget can be set.

exceptions.name: Budget returned by the operations manager
exceptions.description: Fee, contingency or general conditions do not agree with the approved bid, or lines are mis-coded, and the budget is rebuilt.

exceptions.name: No staff free for the team
exceptions.description: A field engineer or assistant superintendent has to be hired or transferred from another region.

exceptions.name: Owner defers the start
exceptions.description: Funding, permits or a land issue hold the start after the contract is signed; the file is parked.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from executed contract to release to mobilize
benchmarks.population: Canadian buildings general contractor, projects of $1-100M, 2019-2022

evidence.note: The source starts the readiness report at least 4 weeks before construction begins; the author adds the week or two between award and the start of readiness work. Treat as a tier C estimate anchored on that practice.

benchmarks.unit: hours of staff time per project start

evidence.note: Sum of the step touch times; no published figure found.

pain_points.description: The estimator has moved on to the next bid, so the turnover package and answers to questions arrive late and incomplete.

evidence.note: Scattered documents and assumptions disconnected from the plan are named as typical handoff failures.

pain_points.description: Scope added during negotiation or verbal promises to the owner are lost between the bid and the contract and resurface later as unbudgeted cost.
The estimate is re-cut into job cost codes by hand in Excel and keyed into the ERP, so the original budget carries coding errors into every cost report.

evidence.note: Common 2019-2022 practice where the estimating and ERP systems were not integrated.

pain_points.description: Superintendents and project managers are released late from finishing jobs, which delays the team's first site walk and logistics plan.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on how general contractors staff from a bench of finishing projects.

sources.title: The Sales-To-Operations Handoff Checklist For General Contractors
sources.supports: What a general contractor hands from sales/estimating to operations: final scope with alternates, exclusions and allowances, commitments made during the pursuit, executed contract, contacts, site and access details, pricing and budget, estimate assumptions on labour, materials, subcontractors, production rates and duration; typical failures are scope drift, lost commitments, scattered documents, assumptions disconnected from the plan and unclear ownership.

sources.title: Project Setup (Brinkmann Constructors process database)
sources.publisher: Procore Technologies support site, Brinkmann Constructors process pages
sources.supports: A project readiness report started at least 4 weeks before the project begins and approved by the regional vice-president before construction starts; project start-up meeting of PM, superintendent and project engineer; kickoff strategy meeting with the director; accounting and project platform setup from a new project setup form.

sources.title: CCDC 2 - 2020 Stipulated Price Contract (standard form text in a District of Hudson's Hope tender package)
sources.publisher: Canadian Construction Documents Committee; document posted by the District of Hudson's Hope
sources.supports: GC 3.4.1: construction schedule submitted to owner and consultant before the first application for payment, showing major activities and critical events, monitored and updated monthly or as the Contract Documents state, consultant advised of revisions from extensions of Contract Time; GC 3.6.1: contractor makes written agreements with subcontractors and suppliers that incorporate the prime contract terms; GC 3.6.2-3.6.3: owner may object to a proposed subcontractor before signing; GC 5.2.4: schedule of values at least 15 calendar days before the first application for payment; GC 9.4.1: contractor establishes, maintains and supervises health and safety precautions and programs; GC 10.4.1: evidence of workers' compensation compliance before commencing the Work and with each application for payment; GC 11.1: contractor insurance per CCDC 41.

sources.title: Construction Buyout Process Guide
sources.supports: Buyout in weekly waves after award (long-lead and early trades in week 1, structure and MEP week 2, interiors week 3, specialties week 4); bulk of buyout takes two to four weeks on a typical commercial project and six to eight weeks on larger ones; verify insurance certificates before signing the subcontract; scope gaps between bids become change orders.

sources.title: Construction Buyout: How GCs Finalize Subcontract Awards After Bid Leveling
sources.supports: Buyout steps after leveling: buyout log, letters of intent for long-lead items (16-36+ week lead times), shortlist of 1-2 subs per package, scope clarification meetings, best and final offers, executed subcontracts; buyout typically takes 2-6 weeks after award, 4-6 weeks with 20+ trade packages; unresolved scope gaps turn into change orders.

assumptions: The case starts at the executed contract and ends at release to mobilize. Buyout, scheduling, safety planning, permits and mobilization are separate processes that start from the startup package and run partly in parallel with the last steps here.
Steps that in practice overlap (meeting attendance, platform setup alongside ERP setup) are listed in sequence with near-zero waits and named in concurrent_with.
The turnover meeting is attended by five people; the step times count the estimator and superintendent only, so labour cost per start is understated by about 6-8 hours of other attendees' time.

The simulated median (about 40 days) is above the 35-day benchmark because the simulation adds every wait in sequence, while in practice the site walk, logistics plan and buyout plan overlap with budget setup. The gap is within the range the benchmark itself is uncertain by.
Readiness sign-off is shown with the operations manager; the Brinkmann source has the regional vice-president approve it, which this organisation reserves for team appointments.
fte_on_process for each role = mean hands-on hours per case from the steps x 10 starts a month / 130 productive hours, plus 25% for coordination not written as steps.
The org file's process roles omit regional-vp (who approves the team) and assistant-pm (who sets up the platform and sends start-of-work documents); both are org roles and are used here.
